title: ORBIT: Oak Ridge Base Foundation Model for Earth System Predictability
problem: Earth system predictability is challenged by the complexity of environmental dynamics and multitude of variables. Current AI foundation models are constrained by their size and data integration, limiting their effectiveness in addressing Earth system prediction challenges.
motivation: Improving Earth system predictability through scaling foundation models is critical for addressing complex environmental dynamics that current AI systems cannot adequately handle.
method: ORBIT is a vision transformer model scaled to 113 billion parameters using a novel hybrid tensor-data orthogonal parallelism technique. Performance scaling tests on the Frontier supercomputer across 49,152 AMD GPUs demonstrated sustained throughput of 684 petaFLOPS to 1.6 exaFLOPS with scaling efficiency of 41% to 85%.
key_novelty: A hybrid tensor-data orthogonal parallelism technique enabling vision transformers to scale to 113 billion parameters for Earth system prediction, surpassing prior climate AI models by 1000x.
contributions: Scaled vision transformer to 113 billion parameters, 1000x larger than existing climate AI foundation models
Novel hybrid tensor-data orthogonal parallelism technique for efficient distributed training
Achieved 684 petaFLOPS to 1.6 exaFLOPS sustained throughput on Frontier supercomputer
Demonstrated 41-85% scaling efficiency across 49,152 AMD GPUs

metrics.other: 684 petaFLOPS to 1.6 exaFLOPS sustained throughput, 41-85% scaling efficiency

primary_theme: Large-scale vision transformer for Earth system prediction with hybrid parallelism
